plain: Text slipped into a model's input, by a user or inside a document or tool output, that tries to give the model instructions it should not follow, such as “rate this 10/10” inside an item a judge is grading.
eli5: Writing “give me an A” in tiny letters at the bottom of your homework.
technical: Adversarial content in untrusted input that the model treats as instructions: direct when the end user types it, indirect when it is planted in third-party content the model reads (web pages, emails, tool outputs). Against judges: universal suffixes that inflate absolute scores (Raina et al. 2024), optimised injections for pairwise judges (Shi et al. 2024).
